newsitem.title: USA: Richmond Fed official sees inflation warning sign.
newsitem.headline: Richmond Fed official sees inflation warning sign.

text.p: Manufacturing prices rose across the board in the latest regional economic survey by the Richmond Federal Reserve Bank, raising some concern about the inflation outlook, a Richmond Fed economist said on Tuesday.
"Prices pretty much across the board increased," Raymond Owens told Reuters Financial Television.
"That is something we have not seen before for a long, long while," he added. "Perhaps it does raise at least a small flag to focus a bit more attention on what is going on on the price side."

In the Richmond Fed's June survey, manufacturing companies reported increases in both the prices they paid for materials and the prices they received for their products. They also foresaw prices rising further in the future.
While service companies did not report higher prices in June, they also forecast sharp price increases in the months ahead, Owens noted.

"Our producers across all sectors are looking for demand to hold up and as a consequence perhaps they're looking for some increased prices pressures as we look forward," Owens said. "Down the road people are relatively optimistic."

Owens described growth in the manufacturing industry in the Richmond Fed region as "robust" and "healthy" but said it was not accelerating. "Growth ... continues but it certainly isn't picking up at this point," he said.
Manufacturing companies again reported that they were holding more inventory than they wanted, but Owens said the survey showed that stock levels were moving "toward a more comfortable range."
On the retail side, sales looked to have rebounded in June, although sales of big-ticket items fell. That may be indicative of the trend nationwide, Owens said.
Wages in the survey seem to be holding steady, according to Owens.
"We're still not seeing an increase in wage pressures," he said, calling that development "interesting" given the tightness of labor markets.
The Richmond Fed region includes Washington, D.C., Maryland, North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia and most of West Virginia.
